selection: Purposive archetype diversity using official conference recognition plus a systems paper; not exhaustive and not acceptance-predictive.

notes.title: Privacy Auditing with One (1) Training Run
notes.paper_archetype: theory with algorithm and empirical validation
notes.selection_basis: NeurIPS 2023 outstanding main-track paper; official award announcement
locators: Section 1 and 1.1; HTML lines 49–67
Section 2, Algorithm 1 and accompanying explanation; lines 68–93
original_observations: The introduction distinguishes mathematical privacy upper bounds from empirical audit lower bounds before posing the computational question.
The contribution preview separates procedure, analysis, and observed result. Algorithm inputs and abstention are explained in adjacent prose.
notes.transferable_move: Define the precise question and the kind of evidence that answers it before introducing the mechanism. Separate complementary contributions without multiplying module names.
notes.transfer_limit: The sampled arXiv version is not asserted to equal the final proceedings version; theoretical proofs and full experiments were not reviewed.

notes.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
notes.selection_basis: NeurIPS 2023 outstanding main-track paper; official award announcement
locators: PDF text: Introduction on printed page 2
Section 2; Figure 2 caption on printed page 3; equations/assumptions on printed page 4
PDF text lines 33–241
original_observations: The paper states an alternative account and enumerates complementary predictions/tests.
A mathematical illustration and panel-by-panel caption connect metric transformations to apparent discontinuity; an independence approximation is identified in the derivation.
notes.transferable_move: Make rival accounts and their discriminating predictions explicit; make a figure caption carry the inferential steps.
notes.transfer_limit: Caption and extracted text were read, not the figure image; no conclusion about all possible emergence phenomena follows from this writing study.

notes.title: The PRISM Alignment Dataset: What Participatory, Representative and Individualised Human Feedback Reveals About the Subjective and Multicultural Alignment of Large Language Models
notes.selection_basis: NeurIPS 2024 datasets-and-benchmarks best paper; official award announcement
locators: Section 1 and start of Section 2; Figure 1 caption; HTML lines 165–195
Section 3.2 methods/results and Section 3.3 methods/Figure 5 caption; lines 255–270
Appendix navigation B, T, U, V; headings only
original_observations: The overview distinguishes participants, conversations, interactions, and utterances, linking each to the collection process.
Case studies pose separate questions and include methods, results, and bounded interpretation; ranking sensitivity is directly discussed.
notes.transferable_move: Explain resource units and show specific research uses rather than making size the entire argument.
notes.transfer_limit: Appendix headings were inspected for navigation; appendix contents were not reviewed. Population representativeness is not implied beyond stated samples.

notes.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
notes.selection_basis: Systems diversity exemplar; no award claim
locators: Introduction excerpt, Figure 2 caption; HTML lines 67–95
Section 5.1–5.2 excerpts and Sections 6.1–6.3; lines 238–298
original_observations: The introduction quantifies a bottleneck before explaining the paging analogy.
Evaluation documents reconstructed baselines and oracle variants, links throughput to batching, and explains a weaker-benefit workload using a competing compute bottleneck.
notes.transferable_move: Write a workload-dependent operating envelope and distinguish implemented, reconstructed, and idealized comparators.
notes.transfer_limit: The explanation of a regime boundary is an author interpretation; this reading does not independently verify causation or measurements.

notes.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
notes.selection_basis: ICLR 2025 outstanding paper; official award announcement
locators: v4 Section 2.2 estimation paragraph; Section 3.2 numerical-threshold footnote and equations 9–10
v2 Sections 2.1–3.2; HTML lines 84–140
v2 research questions and Table 1/setup; lines 176–213
original_observations: The method develops the preservation constraint before the computational projection.
The text distinguishes unavailable complete knowledge from an estimate and uses a numerical eigenvalue threshold.
notes.transferable_move: Explicitly map an exact identity to the sampled and approximate implementation; state which guarantee survives each substitution.
notes.transfer_limit: This is a critical writing lesson, not an independent proof audit. The reading must not turn an exact null-space identity into universal preservation of all model knowledge.

notes.title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep
notes.selection_basis: ICLR 2025 outstanding paper; official award announcement
locators: Section 1 and Sections 2.1–2.2 opening; HTML lines 62–92
Section 2.3 end and Sections 3–3.1; lines 152–171
original_observations: A unifying diagnostic notion precedes potential remedies.
The transition into the intervention is framed as a counterfactual question; a token-probability example clarifies why suppressing initial output need not constrain continuations.
notes.transferable_move: Organize a diagnosis around an operational definition, observable consequences, and a discriminating intervention.
notes.transfer_limit: Do not copy the specific unsafe example. The paper’s remedies are evaluated research interventions, not evidence of comprehensive safety.

notes.title: Transformers are Inherently Succinct
notes.selection_basis: ICLR 2026 outstanding paper; official award announcement
locators: Section 1, contributions and assumptions; HTML lines 51–73
Sections 2.4–2.5; lines 170–180
Section 3 Example 4, Theorem 5 and reduction overview; lines 181–242
original_observations: The introduction changes the comparison criterion from recognized language classes to description size.
Size conventions and model restrictions precede the results. A small counter construction introduces the mechanism of a harder reduction.
notes.transferable_move: Introduce the comparison axis, explain why it matters, and use a worked example before a general proof construction.
notes.transfer_limit: Succinctness under stated formal restrictions does not establish trainability, practical performance, or superiority of all deployed transformers.

notes.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
notes.selection_basis: ICLR 2026 outstanding paper; official award announcement
locators: Introduction and related-work contrast; HTML lines 105–125
Section 3.2 end, Section 3.3 and Section 4.1; lines 156–205
original_observations: The related-work distinction explains why episodic conversation tasks miss the targeted setting.
Simulation variants have explicit evidential roles: a concatenated condition retains rephrasing while removing the multi-turn condition. Simulator errors are discussed before interpretation.
notes.transferable_move: Describe each control as resolving a particular alternative explanation and validate transformations used to construct a benchmark.
notes.transfer_limit: Simulated conversations are not automatically representative of live deployment; historical model findings must not become universal present-day claims.

original_observations: The motivation explains why established numerical methods face different requirements in deep learning.
Finite-precision adjustments and offline/online computation are explicit. Numerical convergence and downstream training evidence answer different questions.
notes.transferable_move: Connect ideal analysis, numerical stabilization, component behavior, and end-to-end benefit without treating them as interchangeable evidence.
notes.transfer_limit: The same paper’s versions are one reading record, not two papers. Code text was inspected, not executed or independently reproduced.
